slides.texte_overlay:
Little habits that make you
look effortlessly classy
Keep your shoes clean. Not new, just clean. People look at shoes far more than you think, and a quick wipe before you leave the house says you pay attention to details.
Learn to tie a proper knot. A tie, a scarf, even your shoelaces. Knowing two or three classic knots makes simple outfits look deliberate instead of thrown together.
Speak a little softer than the room. Classy men rarely need to raise their voice. A calm, slightly lower volume makes people lean in and actually listen to what you say.
Know a little about the things around you. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it makes museums, menus and old buildings far more interesting to talk about.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Museums, menus and old buildings become far more interesting to talk about.

slides.texte_overlay: Hold doors and let people go first. Small courtesies cost nothing. Doing them without making a show of it is one of the most elegant habits a man can have.
Own one good coat. Dark, well cut, the right size. A great coat lifts everything you wear underneath and makes even jeans and a sweater look put together all winter.
Put your phone away at the table. Out of sight, not face down. Giving people your full attention during a meal is rarer and more elegant than any watch or brand.
